items.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: He gained valuable experience in his home town with guitarist Tiny Grimes

ctx.x: Pianist Ray Bryant was born to a musical family in Philadelphia on December 24, 1931. He gained valuable experience in his home town with guitarist Tiny Grimes and as house pianist at the Blue Note. Ray moved to New York in the late 50s and performed and recorded with Carmen McRae, Sonny Rollins, Jo Jones and numerous other jazz luminaries. “Little Susie” and “Cubano Chant”

are among Ray’s original tunes which became popular on his own trio recordings. He tours abroad frequently and enjoys a special status in Japan with fellow pianist Junior Mance. His most recent recording is “Ray’s Tribute to his Jazz Piano Friends.”

items.title: 67425_Tiny Grimes oral history interview
items.q: Some of the other records you did for Prestige included one with Jerome Richardson, Ray Bryant... He was on it and Ray Bryant was on it

ctx.x: [Plays Prelude to a kiss in chords]
What was it like recording for Prestige records in the 50's and 60's?
When you made a recording for Prestige as far as I was concerned they had all the sidemen their own, and they just wanted you to front them.
